subject: Nanotechnology
title: Equity in Nano Access
description: A short lesson to help you apply Equity in Nano Access.

hook.text: Nano medicine could save millions — but only if developing countries can afford it. Who benefits from nano?

buildup.text: Most nano research happens in wealthy nations — the US, EU, China, Japan, and South Korea dominate investment.

discovery.text: Nano water purification and diagnostics could solve problems specific to low-income countries — if deployed there.

twist.text: Patent thickets around nano technologies can block affordable access — intellectual property versus public health.

climax.text: Open-source nano initiatives and technology transfer programs aim to democratize access — nano for all, not just the few.

punchline.text: Nano's promise means nothing if only the wealthy can reach it.

quiz.question: What ethical concern surrounds nanotechnology access in developing countries?
options: Developing countries have too much nanotechnology already
Patent barriers and high costs may prevent those who need nano innovations most from accessing them
Nanotechnology only works in cold climates
